body: We should add the appropriate TORCH_CHECK to ensure these size are correct. Feel free to send a PR fixing this!

Hey it is very much possible that this code was updated on the python side to support more than just the basic case the C++ code supports.
I also missed that these are private functions. So you should not be calling them directly. Are you able to reproduce this segfault when calling only public APIs?

Another thing is, the absence of shape check(of `max_unpool*d`) seems unsafe. Currently any tensor can reach `input_size[d + 2]` and lead to buffer overflow. Existing shape checks([2d](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/2764ead4296541b324ae0e8e2b6200eec0e90c4e/aten/src/ATen/native/MaxUnpooling.cpp#L35-L37), [3d](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/2764ead4296541b324ae0e8e2b6200eec0e90c4e/aten/src/ATen/native/MaxUnpooling.cpp#L91-L93)) are executed after those things.

issue.body:
Fixes #106702 and add some tests

As shown by [maxUnpool1d](https://pytorch.org/docs/master/generated/torch.nn.MaxUnpool1d)(`MaxUnpool2d`, `MaxUnpool3d` also), `Input` and `Output` support `(N,C,*)` or `(C,*)`, but the c++ api currently supports the former, and the latter will cause a coredump.
